messages:
marta: quick follow-up from the routing RFC — we're seeing ambiguity on whether to prefer bucketization (static routing buckets per tenant/workload) vs per-request dynamic scoring. want to align on the API surface and fallbacks.
kevin: short take: buckets are simpler for SLOs and cold-start predictability. dynamic scoring wins for cost-sensitive mixed traffic.
jasper: agree. also ops asks: how do we reason about cache affinity? bucketization -> stronger cache locality, dynamic -> messy KV cache distribution.
sophia: question: can we hybridize? e.g. coarse buckets (region+tier) + dynamic per-request score inside bucket. keeps cache benefits while optimizing cost.
marta: that was one option i sketched. tradeoffs: complexity in policy engine, more state to manage, and rollout risk.
kevin: implementation idea: policy decides bucket_id first (deterministic hash of tenant+route+region preference). then runtime applies a score function limited to candidates in bucket. fallback to global pool if bucket full.
ryan: sounds reasonable. need to define bucket sizing algorithm and overcommit rules. also: what about dedicated customers who expect pinned variants? they should be able to opt-out of scoring and pin to a variant.
jasper: +1 on opt-out. operator story: metrics must show bucket hit rate, pct fallbacks to global, and cost delta. without observability this becomes a nightmare.
sophia: API surface question: do we expose bucket tuning knobs to customers or keep internal? my vote: internal defaults + advanced customer flags for Dedicated.
marta: agreed. keep public surface minimal. but config model must survive rollouts: support canary of bucket changes per-tenant.
kevin: edge case: multi-region failover. if preferred region bucket is down, do we allow cross-region routing in the bucket (we lose cache locality) or instantly fallback to cheaper variant in other region? policy should express priorities: [latency_preferred_region, cost_budget, legal_region_constraints].
jasper: maybe represent policy as ordered constraints rather than monolithic score. ranking pipeline: filter by hard constraints (legal/tenant pins), then score by soft objectives (latency, cost), then pick within bucket.
marta: nice. that lets us keep deterministic steps and easier debugging. we also need a deterministic tiebreaker (hash by request id).
sophia: about the policy engine: do we keep it as a library loaded into runtime or a separate service? library = lower latency, but harder to change policies without deploy. service = dynamic updates but added RPC hop and availability.
kevin: we should prototype both. for Hosted low-latency paths, a library with hot-reloadable policy config + versioned bundles might be best. for Private deployments, we can offer an agent that fetches policies.
ryan: one more point: telemetry and auditing. every routing decision should emit minimal trace: bucket_id, filtered candidates, final choice, policy_version. keep size small but searchable.
deploy-bot: deploy started: routing-policy/v2.3 -> staging (marta,kevin)
marta: thanks. next steps: create small design doc with the ranking pipeline (filter -> soft-score -> bucket selection -> fallback), sketch config model (coarse buckets + in-bucket scoring), and list observability events. i'll drop a draft in #eng-ml for review. :thumbsup:
kevin: i'll add bucket sizing heuristics and a canary rollout plan.
jasper: i'll add cache-affinity metrics and a small sim to estimate cost/latency tradeoffs.
sophia: ok, will review the draft and add customer-facing opt-out wording.
ryan: will wire up tracing proto for the events mentioned.
marta: awesome, thanks all.
